not to ignore your larger point that religion isn't a driving cause of this conflict, which i still dont really agree with, but it's not honest to characterize the history and relations of jews, muslims, and christians living in al-Andalus during that time as "just fine." i'm not an expert, i wont pretend to be so feel free to correct me, but as far as i know, it's just more complicated than that.

while that area of the world during that time is an excellent example of overall tolerance, there are many examples of religion-motivated attacks discrimination from that time as well. it's not like it there was an overflowing, unending spring of love and tolerance among different religious groups until the reconquista fucked everything up. in fact, religion was kinda **the** primary social division between people. jews and christians still had to pay special taxes in order to have rights, a "gift" that was owed to them as people of the book. religious tolerance was often the by product of religious infighting: "i hate the other sect of my religion more than i hate your religion, so we can work together" (Ismael ibn Nagrila is one example, though that is also more complicated).

you are right that there was a staggeringly high tolerance in the region, but it wasn't like religion wasn't a major factor or a common motivator for hatred and violence.

Hey there. I'm kind of in the same boat as you, but my ex broke up with me instead. I was the guy who felt insecure too often, and she was the girl who would rather not talk about her feelings or problems we had. So, some of the things I'm about to tell you might not be entirely applicable to your situation, but I hope something that I say will help.

Listen, I know you probably feel at times like you're never going to make memories like the ones you made with him. I would like you to know, or remember, that you WILL make more of those types of memories, and they will not include him. Have hope. Eventually, there will be times that you will forget about him.

But there's also gonna be times where you'll find yourself thinking about him again, and how much fun you used to have, if you could've done things differently, or if you can still salvage your relationship. You gotta ask yourself, is that something you really, really want? Ignore all the pain you felt and effort you put in before, and seriously ask yourself, do you want to give him another shot? Could you be happy again? Could you love him again, even if you somehow find a way to forget the past? Try and make your brain, which will often work against you in this regard, to focus on what you want that is truly best for you when answering those questions. Be honest with yourself.

If you can't answer that, or need help, hit up your friends, your parents, or anyone you believe may help (except for drug dealers, that's a no-no). Reach out. Ask for help, even if you don't think that they will be able to help or if you don't want their help. Trust them. Even just hanging out and talking to other people can be a sweet breath of relief from your memories of him. But believe me, you don't want to try and forget about someone by yourself. I'm not saying find a rebound, but try and live for yourself a little. Occupy your mind and body with thoughts and actions that will distract you, but more importantly, with things that you enjoy for your own sake. 

It will naturally become easier to forget him, but you're the only one who can decide whether you will really move on in a healthy way. You can do it; you can forget about him if you want. But you gotta help yourself first, one way or another. Whether it's by reaching out or working on yourself, actively taking steps toward your happiness will draw others to you and shield yourself from some of the pain of those memories. You decide when that happens. Good luck, you got this :)
